description.narrative:
icipe is an African-initiated, based and led Centre of Excellence within insect and arthropod science. icipe has research and outreach activities in more than 40 African countries, including in Norway’s five priority countries for food security; Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, Ghana and South Sudan. It also has activity in DRC Congo, Somalia, and the Sahel, which are of importance to Norad’s portfolio on food security.
The expected impact of the Core Activities is to contribute to poverty alleviation, food security, and human and environmental health in Africa. The expected outcomes of the Core Activities are: - increased productivity, sustainability, and resilience of the agri-food systems in Africa; - enhanced research and development and innovation capacity in Africa; and - increased influence on global and regional insect science and Four-Health policies development processes.
icipe uses a One-Health approach to its research integrating four Health Themes: Plant Health, Animal Health, Environmental Health, and Human Health. icipe’s research and development agenda is aimed at contributing to reducing climate impact and strengthening resilience to climate change. It carries out research to fill critical knowledge gaps on climate change impact on ecosystem services and invasive pests and deploys climate-smart technologies.
Gender equality is among icipe’s key values. It strives to empower women in its own workforce and applies gender equity principles across its programs, capacity building initiatives and by influencing policy and its partners.
